title: Sales Enablement: Positioning, Competitive Briefs, Pitch Decks, Pricing & Security FAQ
author: Jordan Patel
body:
Summary
This playbook consolidates Redwood Inference's go-to-market assets for sales and solutions teams: core positioning and messaging, competitive battlecards, a recommended pitch deck outline, pricing guidance by customer profile, short case studies for prospect conversations, and a security FAQ tailored for procurement and security reviewers. Use this doc as the canonical source for deck content, objection responses, and pre-sales enablement.

Audience
- AEs (small-mid-enterprise)
- Solutions Engineers and Pre-Sales
- Sales Engineers and Channel Partners
- Customer Success (for expansion conversations)

1) Positioning & Messaging
Objective: Communicate Redwood's unique value quickly (30-60s) and expand into a short story for technical and executive stakeholders.

Elevator pitch (customer-facing):
Redwood Inference provides a unified inference platform that makes it easy to deploy, optimize, and operate LLMs with predictable latency, transparent unit economics, and enterprise-grade controls across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments.

Three-line technical pitch:
- High-throughput serving runtime optimized for GPU inference, continuous batching, and KV cache management.
- Smart routing and model variants for cost and availability: route by latency, cost, region, and customer tier.
- Observability and controls (per-route cost breakdown, rollouts, and automatic fallbacks) to run LLMs in production with predictable economics.

Key value props (by persona)
- Product/Engineering: Fast integration (REST/SDK), predictable latency SLOs, and rollout controls to ship features without building an inference stack.
- Platform/SRE: Centralized observability, cost tooling, and dedicated GPU pools to maintain SLAs and forecasting.
- Security/Legal: Private deployment options (VPC/on-prem), KMS/HSM support, and audit logging for regulated workloads.

Proof points / metrics to use
- Average P95 text-generation latency (hosted API): 80-150ms (varies by model/seq length) — include per-model benchmark slides from the model catalog.
- Unit economics: case example — 35% token-cost reduction using caching and batching on chat-heavy workloads (Customer: Acme Health, see case study).
- Reliability: 99.95% uptime target for Dedicated customers with SLA-backed support.

2) Competitive Briefs (short battlecards)
Structure for competitor win/loss conversations:
- Competitor name
- Typical customer use cases they win
- Redwood strengths vs. them (3-5 bullets)
- Primary risk/weakness to communicate (3 bullets)
- Suggested talking points and proof artifacts (benchmarks, case studies, pricing comparison)

Example: Competitor: CloudAI Endpoints
- They win: quick model hosting for small proof-of-concepts, strong marketplace reach.
- Redwood strengths: predictable production economics (batching/caching), dedicated capacity for enterprise SLAs, unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private deployments.
- Risks: CloudAI has deeper marketplace integrations and larger ecosystem; Redwood should emphasize controlled rollouts + lower TCO on medium-to-high QPS workloads.
- Talking points: cite our 3-month pilot with Acme Health (20% latency improvement vs. CloudAI using dedicated pools), pricing comparison (below) and demo of the rollouts console.

Top competitor differentiators to call out in calls
- Pure-hosted API vendors: emphasize single-runtime across private/dedicated and cost levers.
- Self-hosted runtime vendors: emphasize Redwood's managed operational tooling, observability, and security integrations.
- Cloud providers (managed endpoints): emphasize model-choice neutrality, lower inference unit cost at scale with caching and quantization profiles.

3) Pitch Deck: Recommended slide flow and template snippets
Use a concise 10-15 slide deck for discovery and an extended 20-30 slide deck for technical deep dives. Keep one-sentence messages per slide and include customer-proof slides early in the deck for credibility.

10-slide discovery deck (recommended flow)
1. Title / customer logo (personalize)
2. Executive TL;DR / 30-60s pitch
3. Customer pain and opportunity (customize with prospect KPIs)
4. Redwood value props (3 bullets)
5. Product demo screenshots / architecture (hosted vs. dedicated vs. private)
6. Case study highlight (metric-driven)
7. Security & compliance snapshot
8. Pricing & engagement options (summary)
9. Next steps / pilot proposal
10. Appendix (benchmarks, integrations)

Slide notes: include demo checklist (test prompts, target latency queries, SSO/KMS proofs) and a technical appendix with API examples and model performance tables. Attach our standard pilot SOW template (link in related pages).

4) Pricing Guidance (rules of thumb)
Principles
- Keep pricing conversations focused on value: SLA, latency, and cost per inference.
- Offer clear pilots with time-limited discounts and upgrade paths to dedicated capacity.
- Be transparent about unit economics drivers: sequence length, batching, cache-hit rates, and model choice.

Suggested pricing tiers (guidance only; reference legal for quotes)
- Self-Serve / Trial: usage-based, per-token pricing with free credits and rate limits.
- Growth (small-mid market): monthly committed usage with discounts (10-25%) and basic SLOs.
- Enterprise / Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved capacity, SLA-backed, enterprise support, private deployment add-ons.

Example pilot offer (for AEs/SEs to use)
- 8-week pilot: $0 setup fee, $Xk in credits (negotiable by ARR potential), 2-week extension option based on traction.
- Deliverables: pilot runbook, custom prompt set, baseline & post-optimization cost/latency report, and a recommendation for dedicated capacity sizing.

Pricing objections & responses
- "Your pricing is higher than the pure-hosted vendor": Explain total cost of ownership — transparent token breakdown, lower operational effort, and lower latency/TCO at scale thanks to caching/quantization. Offer a pilot-to-dedicated cost projection.
- "We can't commit to long-term reserved capacity": propose hybrid model (growth tier with burstable reserved capacity) and demonstrate autoscaling controls.

5) Case Studies (two short vignettes for sales use)
Case study: Acme Health (Healthcare SaaS) - Context: HIPAA-sensitive triage assistant using clinical notes to generate triage recommendations.
- Solution: Private deployment (VPC) with KMS integration, dedicated pools for daytime peak load, and prefix caching for frequent prompts.
- Outcome: 45% reduction in average inference cost per session, P95 latency improved from 320ms to 140ms after quantization and KV caching, go-live in 9 weeks.
- What to emphasize: security posture (private deploy + audit logs), speed-to-production, and measurable cost improvements.

Case study: FinServe (Retail Banking chatbot)
- Context: customer service chatbot with heavy conversational context (long histories).
- Solution: Dedicated capacity with KV cache and proactive batching optimization; model quantization profile for mid-tier models.
- Outcome: 30% reduction in resolved-contact time, 22% decrease in agent-hand-off rate, 18% token cost reduction month-over-month.
- What to emphasize: throughput predictability, lower mean time to resolution, and smooth canary rollouts during peak campaigns.

6) Security FAQ for Prospects (concise answers for procurement/security reviewers)
Q: Do you support VPC/private deployments and on-premises options?
A: Yes. Redwood supports VPC peering and a private deployment model with a customer-managed control plane. We also offer an on-prem package for fully air-gapped environments under enterprise agreements.

Q: How is data protected in transit and at rest?
A: All traffic is TLS 1.2+ in transit. Data at rest is encrypted using AES-256. For private deployments, customers can bring their own KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure KeyVault) or use an HSM integration.

Q: Do you have formal certifications?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II (production services) and is pursuing ISO 27001 certification; for regulated customers we provide evidence packages and can support HIPAA BAAs.

Q: How do you handle customer model/data isolation?
A: Dedicated pools and private deployments provide tenant isolation. We support network segmentation, role-based access controls (RBAC), and per-customer audit logs. Model artifacts can be stored in customer-controlled storage for private deployments.

Q: What logging and audit capabilities are available?
A: Audit logs include API calls, role changes, and model rollout events. Logs can be forwarded to customer SIEM via secure connectors (S3, GCS, or syslog) and retained per customer retention policies.

Q: How do you manage keys and secrets?
A: We integrate with common KMS providers and support customer-managed keys (CMKs). Secrets are stored encrypted in the control plane and rotate per security policy.

Q: What is your incident response posture?
A: Redwood follows a documented incident response playbook with on-call rotas, security runbooks, and SLA-driven communications. We provide post-incident reports for customers as part of enterprise SLAs.

Q: Can you run on air-gapped infrastructure?
A: Yes — our on-prem package supports air-gapped deployments; the delivery model includes an installation checklist, offline upgrade procedures, and verification scripts.

Operational playbook for pilots (short checklist)
1. Intake: collect prospect app profile (QPS, sequence length, P95 target, compliance requirements).
2. Design: recommend hosted vs. dedicated vs. private and proposed model family.
3. Setup: create pilot project, allocate tokens/credits, configure SSO and KMS as needed.
4. Baseline: run canonical prompt set & capture latency + cost baseline (72h).
5. Optimize: apply batching/caching/quantization recommendations; run A/B prompts.
6. Report: deliver baseline + optimized report; recommended next step (dedicated sizing or production rollout).
7. Close: convert to committed contract or plan phased rollout.

Appendix: Pre-built rebuttal snippets for common objections
- "We need lower latency than you provide": "Let's run a short POC where we simulate your production traffic. We typically hit P95 targets by tuning batching, cache policies and — if needed — dedicated pools. See the Acme Health benchmark in Appendix."
- "We can't expose customer data to hosted services": "We offer private deployments and VPC options; in addition, audit logs and KMS integrations meet enterprise controls."
